messages:
anya: pushed thermo3b-int4 (int4/group64) candidate to staging for redteam + safety eval. quick findings:
- soft-refusal rate ↓6% on toxic_prompts
- jailbreak success ↑0.9% on contrived-instruct set
- latency +12ms vs fp16

sam: can you paste the short table? which cohorts flipped?

ravi: quick paste of metrics from the runner (summary):
```
model,soft_refusal_pct,jailbreak_success_pct,latency_ms
thermo3b-fp16,12.4,1.2,38
thermo3b-int4,11.6,2.1,50
```

anya: raw traces show a few sequences where prefix tokens are stripped before KV cache warmup, so the cache hits are bad and generation goes off-distribution on adversarial prompts.

jin: saw a retry spike in staging logs at ~1768888894, correlates with longer tails. linking logs: https://staging-logs/xyz (perm - staging/thermo3b-int4)

sam: oh ok — so both safety (jailbreak) and perf regressions. do we have ablation per-tensor vs per-channel quant?

ravi: starting a per-channel run now with kvcache warmup enabled. command: `scripts/run_safety_eval.sh --model thermo3b-int4 --quant pcq64 --warmup true --cohorts contrived,instruction,persona`

safety-bot: redteam run finished (auto): 4 cohorts, 1,200 prompts, report uploaded -> https://drive/reports/thermo3b-int4-redteam-1768888888.pdf :rotating_light:

anya: skim of the pdf: most jailbreaks are short-context instruction chains that exploit compressed attention patterns post-quant. notable: refusal wording softened in many cases (more pragmatic answers).

sam: can we add a regression gate: block rollout if jailbreak_success_pct > 1.5% or soft_refusal_pct drops > 4% relative to baseline?

anya: yes. I'll file the CI rule/PR. also we should snapshot the exact quant kernels used (ravi pls).

ravi: kernel/build: kblast-v2 + group-quant64, compiled at commit 0f3b9c. reproducing locally now. initial hypothesis: per-tensor grouping with disabled warmup loses prefix alignment.

jin: action item for oncall: monitor retry storms during next rolls. i'll add a short monitor to paging policies for staging.

sam: also add a tiny eval that checks refusal phrasing diffs (we saw "I can't help with that" -> "Here's an alternative" which is a policy concern).

anya: action items recap:
- ravi: triage quant kernels + reproduce + try per-channel variant (EOD)
- sam: add regression tests + CI gate for jailbreak/soft-refusal thresholds
- jin: monitoring + retry spike watch on staging
- anya: run an extended redteam with per-channel runs once ravi has kernels

ravi: ack. will upload trace snippets and kernel perf logs to the report when done.

sam: thanks team — tagging this for the safety board sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
